summary: Closure ran against the patched copy. All 18 assertions passed: the full regression set re-passed, query-string variants behaved as predicted (a traversal with a query returned 404 and an ordinary nested file with a query returned 200 with a matching body hash), a sibling directory sharing a long name prefix returned 404, and 20 concurrent requests, half leak attempts and half controls, were fully consistent. A separate run with a relative root under a changed working directory kept the gate effective. Symlink behavior was measured rather than assumed: a directory symlink inside the root served outside content with 200 on both vulnerable and patched copies, while a file symlink returned 500 on both; no marker bytes leaked from the file case. The minimal string-containment repair was retained and the symlink behavior documented as a pre-existing, behavior-preserving limitation. A unified diff and a machine-readable patch record were packaged.
next_hint: The minimal containment repair and its regression evidence are ready. An external official harness must still run the packaged patch; if its hidden tests treat a symlink inside the root as in scope, realpath hardening would be required, otherwise the minimal gate is the recommended repair.
